answer: Admission requires buying one undivided cubic-meter water entitlement, metered at a numbered basalt weir whose staff plate is forbidden to back a second account. The hydrology office stores a kernel hash of that plate plus an ultrasonic discharge reading, and later accepts only photographs of the same engraved serial. Reusing the weir or failing a surprise gauge check confiscates the bond. The mountain grove's springs have a hard physical yield, so each alias demands another entitlement bought at auction—an outlay that scales linearly and steepens as unsold shares dwindle.
